name: Create profiles table linked to auth.users with role and hostel scope
w: profiles is the identity root: every row in the product will be scoped to it, so this shape must be correct before any other table exists. A mistake here is a cross-tenant data leak, which is commercially unrecoverable.
ac: profiles has id equal to auth.users.id, plus full_name, phone, role, hostel_id and created_at
Foreign key to auth.users with ON DELETE CASCADE
A database trigger creates a profile row for each new signup
role is constrained to owner, staff or platform_admin
Inserting a profile for an unrelated user is rejected
The signup trigger always assigns role 'owner'; role is never read from user-supplied signup metadata
out: No profile editing UI and no avatar upload in this task.

name: Implement hostel owner signup flow
w: This is where a paying customer meets the product. It must create exactly one identity, land the owner in onboarding rather than an empty dashboard, and never confirm whether an email address is already registered.
ac: Email and password signup with server-side validation from the shared Zod schemas
Duplicate email returns one clear, non-enumerating message
Email confirmation state handled explicitly
Exactly one profile row exists per signup
New owner is redirected into hostel onboarding (a placeholder route until E3-T3 lands), not the dashboard
Confirmation emails work locally through the mail catcher; staging delivery depends on custom SMTP (E9-T4)
out: No social login, no staff invitation flow and no phone OTP.

name: Implement login and logout
w: Owners use the product daily and from shared devices. Login must be fast and logout must genuinely end the session on that device.
ac: Invalid credentials return one generic error message
Session survives a page reload
Logout clears cookies and redirects protected routes to login
An already-authenticated user visiting the login page is redirected away
out: No remember-me, no MFA and no device management.

name: Implement session-aware route middleware
w: Route protection must happen before any data fetching. If an unauthenticated request can still trigger a server query, data can leak through error messages or timing even when the page redirects.
ac: Unauthenticated requests to any route in the (app) group (/dashboard, /rooms, /residents and so on) redirect to /login with a next parameter
Authenticated users are redirected away from auth pages
Session cookies are refreshed on navigation
No database query executes before the session check in a protected route
The next parameter accepts only same-site relative paths, so it cannot be used as an open redirect
Middleware is not the only guard: protected layouts, pages and every server action re-check the user with getUser()
out: No IP allow-listing or rate limiting on login in the MVP.

name: Enable RLS on profiles and write base policies
w: RLS is the only thing standing between two hostels' data. Enabling it here and proving the policies is a gate: every later table copies this pattern.
ac: RLS is enabled on profiles, verified against pg_class.relrowsecurity
A user can select their own profile and update only full_name and phone; changing role or hostel_id is rejected by column privileges or a trigger
Staff can read peers within the same hostel only
The anonymous role is denied all access
Negative tests fail before the policies and pass after, using the anon key
Policies use (select auth.uid()) so it is evaluated once per statement, not per row
out: No platform-admin bypass policy; that belongs to backlog epic EP-10. Staff accounts for the tests are created through the service role.

name: Implement role guard helper for owner, staff and platform admin
w: Permissions must be enforced on the server. A UI-only check is decoration, because anyone can call the underlying server action directly.
ac: requireRole() is usable from server actions and route handlers
An unauthorised call throws before any database write occurs
Platform-admin capability exists as a flag but exposes no UI yet
Unit tests cover owner, staff and unauthorised for at least two actions
out: No permission matrix UI and no custom roles per hostel.

name: Add password reset flow
w: Owners get locked out of their accounts. Without a self-service reset every lockout becomes a manual support incident that you have to handle personally.
ac: Reset email is delivered through Supabase Auth
A valid token sets a new password and invalidates old sessions
Expired or reused tokens show a friendly, non-technical error
The flow does not reveal whether an email address is registered
Works locally through the mail catcher and on staging through custom SMTP
out: No admin-triggered password reset; that is EP-10.
